Subject: Embedded invite broken in our mobile app webview - Accept button causes white screen

Hi Lauren,

We're trying to complete our supplier onboarding for Redwood via the Coupa invite link that your team sent. When our procurement team taps the 'Accept' button inside our mobile ERP app (it's an embedded webview), the overlay goes white and the accept never completes. Clicking the same invite link from a desktop browser works fine.

What we've observed:
- The accept confirmation modal opens, but immediately the view flashes white for ~2s and then returns to the app with no completion state.
- We captured a short screen recording and the browser console from the device. Attaching those files: accept_crash_video.mp4, console_log_20260818.txt.
- This is only happening inside the in-app webview on Android devices (v11/12). iOS looks OK for a few testers but we haven't fully validated.

Customer impact: procurement cannot finish vendor setup, PO visibility is blocked for new suppliers. They're asking for an ETA to fix.

Could you help triage or advise a workaround? Opening the link in an external browser is a workable temporary solution, but we need a better fix for the in-app experience (our users expect to complete onboarding without leaving the ERP).

Thanks,
Alicia Moreno
Sr. Procurement Ops | CinderBeam

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear repro and the recordings, that helps a lot. Looping in Ben (engineering) and Monica (CS) to take a look.

Couple of quick asks to speed triage:
- Can you confirm the tenant_id/organization id that the invite targets (or paste the invite URL)?
- Which exact Android app version and WebView engine (Chromium version) are you running? If you can share the user-agent string from your console dump that’ll be helpful.
- If possible, a HAR from the webview during the accept flow would be ideal (I see you attached a console log; if you can record a HAR that would let us see redirects and cookies).

Workaround for now: please instruct affected users to "Open in browser" (long-press link) instead of using the in-app flow — that bypasses the webview restrictions. We'll prioritize a fix if Ben confirms a server-side route to avoid top-frame redirects.

Ben / Monica — initial notes: video shows the accept modal initiating a top-level redirect (window.top.location) immediately after the POST. If the webview sandbox blocks top-level navigation or third-party cookies are blocked due to SameSite flags, that could produce the white-screen behavior. I flagged INF-8721 for tracking.

I'll update Alicia once we have the repro steps.

Thanks,

Thanks for the context, Lauren and Alicia. I dug into the artifacts Alicia attached. Quick triage notes: 

- The console log shows a blocked navigation error referencing "Blocked top-frame navigation in sandboxed iframe" and a SameSite cookie warning for our session cookie (Set-Cookie: Redwood-Session; SameSite=Lax) at the time of the POST response. In many embedded webviews the default browser policy prevents top-level navigations initiated from an iframe when sandbox attributes are present.
- The HAR shows a short series: POST /invites/accept -> 302 -> GET /onboard/complete -> but the webview never executes the final GET (white frame).

Immediate mitigation (short term):
1) On the frontend invite flow, change the accept flow to respond with a 200 and a small JS payload that calls postMessage to the parent (instead of an immediate top-level redirect). We'll add a fallback that opens the completion URL in a new window when postMessage is not available. This avoids top-frame navigation from inside an iframe.
2) Server-side, set Redwood-Session cookie SameSite=None; Secure so the cookie is permitted in cross-site contexts (we need to audit cookie usage to validate there are no security regressions).

I'll open a focused internal task and push a patch to a canary early tomorrow. Action items for CinderBeam: if you can provide one successful HAR from an external browser and one failing HAR from the embedded webview (same invite link), we can run an A/B to verify. Also, please confirm the app's webview chromium build (we saw a mismatch between 93 and 102 in the console).

I'll update INF-8721 and include the plan and ETA. Tentative ETA for a canary patch is 48 hours pending QA.

Ben Carter
